book: Agrawal ExamCart, SSB OIR, Reasoning section
scans: SSR OIR 1-127 (phone photos of printed pages 1-127)
title: Counting Figures
note: Figures are redrawn (D29), not cut from the photos: each is a list of straight lines and circles, checked line by line against its photo on an overlay sheet. Q1-20 are in the photo's own pixel coordinates; the rest are on an exact grid. `stem` describes the figure in words for screen readers. Q9 prints one small square shaded; it is drawn plain, as shading does not change the count. Q2 is too small in the photo to read every line, Q30's squares cannot be told from its rectangles, and Q37 is drawn in arcs: those three carry no figure. Q35-50 each print their own question, kept as its direction.

questions.stem: A long rectangle with both diagonals and two inner verticals, and a triangle on each short side split by a line from its point to the side's middle.
A square leaning into a point at its foot, with a shaded half-circle on its left and small boxes inside; too small in the photo to read every line.
A square holding a V from its top corners to the middle of its base; from the middle of the top, lines run to the ends of two crossbars of the V.
A rectangle halved across and split by an off-centre vertical, with slanting lines making triangles in each part.
A triangle with a line across it, and a line from the left end of that line to the bottom right corner.
Three overlapping circles over a line across the top two; triangles stand on that line in each top circle, and a triangle hangs below it, split down the middle.
A circle around a rectangle crossed by slanting lines that meet the top middle and a part-way crossbar, with two short verticals below it.
A large square with smaller squares overlapping at three corners down its diagonal: diamonds in the first and last, a V in the middle one.
A house: a triangular roof on a box, divided by verticals and crossbars, with two slanting lines at the bottom. One small square, shaded in the book, is drawn plain.
A circle around a square criss-crossed by horizontals, verticals and slanting lines.
Seven small squares, each cut by a diagonal, joined by a stepped path of lines.
A rectangle with both diagonals between two triangles, one above and one below, each halved by a line from its point.
A square holding overlapping smaller squares and rectangles, with slanting lines making triangles at the corners and edges.
A rectangle in six equal parts, two rows of three, with one diagonal across the whole.
A rectangle in three parts, crossed by a zigzag from the bottom left corner to the top right corner.
A large square overlapped at its top left corner by a small square holding a diamond, and filled with overlapping smaller squares and slanting lines.
A trapezium divided by verticals, crossbars and slanting lines that meet in the middle, with a small triangle in each bottom corner.
A square and a sloping strip side by side, cut into triangles by diagonals, with a column of three boxes hanging down on the right, two of them halved by a diagonal.
A large square with smaller squares overlapping at three corners down its diagonal: a diamond in the first and last, a V in the middle one.
Two arms meeting in a V over a small circle; each arm runs through three arrowheads, each arrowhead a triangle split by the arm.
A square cut into nine by two lines each way, crossed by both its diagonals, which run on into a small square at each corner.
A square cut into nine, holding two tilted squares down its diagonal, each with a smaller tilted square inside.
A square filled with a lattice of slanting lines making tilted squares, with a small triangle flag at each corner.
Two grids of squares, three columns by five rows and six columns by three rows, joined along the bottom by a row of seven squares.
Squares and tilted squares nested inside each other, five deep, crossed by a vertical and a horizontal line through the centre.
An irregular block of squares: a grid four wide and three deep, with squares added on the left, below, and in a column on the right.
A square in a four by four grid with some of its inner lines left out.
A square with both diagonals, a tilted square joining the middles of its sides, and a square inside that.
A staircase of squares, four, three and two high, crossed by slanting lines.
Seven overlapping squares and rectangles of different sizes, with a circle among them.
A house: a rectangle with a roof, a line across it, and a V from its top corners to the middle of its base.
A low rectangle, a wide rectangle beside it, and a tall thin rectangle standing through the wide one.
A rectangle with a smaller rectangle overlapping each of its corners.
A tall rectangle crossed by a short bar near its top and standing on a long base rectangle.
A wide rectangle cut by a line across, beside a tall strip on the right with two slanting lines meeting at its left side.
Two rectangles side by side joined by a bar overlapping both, with an arrow pointing out of each, its shaft a small rectangle.
A square holding a quarter circle and smaller arcs, with half-circles on its outside edges.
A square holding a large circle, a rectangle, a tilted square and a small circle, all centred, with a vertical and a horizontal line through the centre.
Ten circles: a small circle in the middle inside a larger one, ringed by eight overlapping circles.
Thirteen circles: a flower of seven overlapping circles with six more around it.
A square with a tilted square joining the middles of its sides, and a vertical and a horizontal line through the centre.
A hexagon cut in half across its middle and into four by verticals, each part halved by a slanting line.
Two squares side by side, each with both diagonals, with a triangle standing on each top side and hanging from each bottom side.
A square filled with a lattice of slanting lines through the thirds of its sides.
A square cut by three verticals and one horizontal, with both its diagonals and a tilted square joining the middles of its sides.
A strip of three squares, each crossed by both its diagonals.
A rectangle with both diagonals.
A rectangle with both diagonals and a vertical and a horizontal line through its centre.
